old_title: Arsenal v Aston Villa, London City Lionesses v Manchester City, and more: Women's Super League - live
new_title: Charlton 0-6 Chelsea, West Ham 4-1 Liverpool, Birmingham City 1-4 Tottenham, and more: as it happened
old_text:
48 min: Emily Fox and Lisa Baum are on for Arsenal. (At half-time, that is.) Fox was welcomed to the action with a strong shoulder charge by Grant as she advanced into the Villa area.
Half-time: London City Lionesses 0-0 Manchester City Women
Goalless down in Bromley. The hosts have had no fewer than 12 attempts on goal. City have had four, and Mary Earps has made a couple of very handy stops to keep them out.
Grant's goal the difference in the first half. Villa have had one shot, and scored one goal. "The Arsenal" have had five shots on target, it says here. Feels like more. They've had 12 attempts in total.
38 min: Russo has the ball again in the penalty area. She flops to the floor, in the general vicinity of the Villa defender Mathilde Harviken, but it looks like she lost her balance rather than it being a foul.
37 min: Grant nearly breaks through again for Villa, with Arsenal pushing up the field yet again. Catley just manages to pull off a well-timed tackle to snuff out the danger. That was very nearly a one-on-one for Grant and potentially 2-0.
34 min: Does another big team talk await for Slegers at the break? Arsenal have looked the better side by far, but Villa's rope-a-dope strategy has worked to perfection with half time looming.
31 min: The hosts pour forward again, barely able to believe that they are trailing after enjoying so much possession and territory in the first half an hour. Batlle is fed by Stanway, and fashions another good cross from the Arsenal right, but no one is there to meet it for Slegers' side.
28 min: Géraldine Reuteler, almost immediately, has the chance to get Arsenal back level. But she scuffs her shot from around the penalty spot, and throws her head back in frustration.
Chasity Grant, the Dutchwoman, is released down the Villa right. Arsenal are cut open for the first time. Catley tries to cover, but Grant cleverly shapes to cut inside, then back out, and hits a low shot that is deflected off Catley into the far corner. A second WSL goal of the season for Grant.
22 min: Taylor Hinds feeds Russo down the left. The prolific forward cuts in, and hits a bending shot that flashes past the far post. Villa cannot contain Russo or her teammates at the moment. That was Playstation football - which I mean as a compliment to Russo - you could see exactly where her intentions were, but Villa were powerless to stop her.
15 min: Villa are being pressed back constantly, and it feels like a matter of time before Arsenal find a route through this defence. Russo continues to link well with Foord down the Gunners' left.
12 min: Russo provides an excellent layoff for Foord, on the left of the penalty area as Arsenal are attacking. Foord has clear sight of goal, but hits a weak shot straight at the keeper.
5 min: Arsenal have started mostly on the front foot in north London and are looking confident in possession, but a clear-cut chance has yet to materialise.
Villa Women have won their past two league games, against Everton last week and Liverpool the week before that. They are hence two wins from eight in the league and sit eighth in the table.
Both teams are in form, then, even if the unstoppable force and the immovable object might be overstating the case.
A group of well-choreographed, fancy-dress-wearing school-age dancers fully embraced the Halloween spirit on Saturday as they boogied to one of Michael Jackson's greatest hits at half-time here. Alas, the match itself was no thriller.
For Manchester United, the only scary thing about this game was how little they tested Courtney Brosnan in Everton's goal in the first 75 minutes as they demonstrated their lack of creativity.
Five mins until kick-off at the Emirates, and elsewhere. Time for a quick news update from yesterday, via Tom Garry, and a stalemate between Everton and Manchester United at Goodison Park.
As Martin Semmens, the London City Lionesses chief executive, sits down is his office he looks like the cat that got the cream. He says he has just learned that the club's Instagram page has generated 34m hits since Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d'Or on Monday evening, and it is only Thursday afternoon. On Sunday two clubs with seven of the top 30 players in the Ballon d'Or rankings will go head-to-head when Manchester City visit Hayes Lane, Bromley. It is, Semmens, says, "awesome for the WSL".
From the outside, it can feel slightly surreal. The independent women's club, owned by the businesswoman Michele Kang, are third in the top flight, two‐and‐a‐half years after finishing eighth in tier two, and Semmens believes signing the world's best player has helped change the mindset of everyone at the club.
The Gunners return to the domestic stage this afternoon by hosting Aston Villa in the WSL: a third consecutive win would shut down any talk of a crisis after their shaky start to the campaign. London City Lionesses take on the joint-leaders, Manchester City Women, in the other 12pm GMT kick-off.
Birmingham City v Tottenham, West Ham v Liverpool and Brighton v Crystal Palace are the 2pm kick-offs: Charlton v Chelsea is the final match on the menu, beginning at 2.30pm. Let's
new_text:
"It was a massive result," said Manchester City's matchwinner, Lauren Hemp, after the 2-1 win against London City Lionesses earlier today. "London City posed us a lot of threats. Very aggressive team, very physical, and we had to try and match that. I think in the first half we were lacking that bit of physicality that we needed. But at the end of the day, we were the most clinical team today. Credit to the girls, we all put in a massive shift, I think we've all got some bumps and bruises.
"It's amazing playing with Bunny [Shaw]. When you've got someone like that in the box, it's incredible. I always know where she's going to be and vice-versa, and it's great to have someone like that in the team. Yeah, massive shift from everyone today."
"Disappointed," Alessia Russo said earlier after Arsenal's 1-1 draw with Villa. "This is a tough league and anyone can take points off of anyone. We know we've got to be better, and we'll reflect on it in the week.
"We know we have so much talent, so many players that can score goals ... but it's just about picking our moments, being a little bit more ruthless, I think we had quite a lot of chances in the first half, and we want to make more of them count."
The BBC show a few replays of the Dragoni goal, that rounded off the scoring at 6-0. It was a quality effort all round: the first touch was with her studs, taking the ball away from the defender, and buying the space to swivel and fire a low shot across the keeper and into the net. Lovely stuff.
Charlton did well to keep it to six, having collapsed to 4-0 down early doors.
Dragoni, who scored the sixth, looks utterly thrilled to have registered her first WSL goal. Her teammates look delighted for her, too. That's nice to see.
90 min + 3: Keira Flannery leaves a foot in on Hamano. That was a naughty one, with studs on the ankle. Hamano shrugs it off like a true pro. There is no yellow card when arguably there should have been.
79 min: Thompson is through for Chelsea. One-on-one with Koivunen. She takes a slightly inaccurate first touch, but sets herself well for the eventual shot ... and blasts it narrowly wide of a post.
75 min: Anna Koivunen makes a stunning stop from Thompson! The ball is floated to the far post, and the debutante Charlton keeper makes herself big to block the shot from point-blank range. Hamano fires over from the rebound. Koivunen has performed admirable despite conceding six.
69 min: Chance for Charlton! McCabe clears an Ash Neville header off the line after a corner. The Addicks immediately pour forward again - this is all very unusual - but have a shot blocked.
Chelsea hit the woodwork not once, but twice ... but no matter. Moments later Giulia Dragoni, the 19-year-old Italian who is fresh off the bench, cracks a low shot unerringly into the far corner. (Maika Hamano and Alyssa Thompson are also on for the Blues.)
What a turnaround! Peskett turns the ball into the net after a bit of pinball in the box! The celebrations are suitably joyous after a quick comeback: two goals in five minutes.
Spurs 3-0 up on Birmingham City, West Ham 3-0 up on Liverpool, Chelsea 4-0 up on Charlton. The only remaining jeopardy, it would seem, is in Brighton v Crystal Palace ... and right on cue there's a goal for Brighton!
One shot, on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch up.
Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo's 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.
40 min: Charlton's defenders won't be sorry that James has gone off. It still promises to be a long afternoon - but James was the creative lynchpin for Chelsea during that four-goal salvo.
If Charlton can make it to half-time at 4-0, they've not conceded for over half an hour. That's actually pretty impressive given how the opening minutes unfolded.
